DeleteCommandTest only runs the command against a real ModelManager,

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command to record attendance
commitResults.messageBody:
TAs need to record whether each student was present or absent at
each weekly tutorial, but there is no way to record attendance.

Let's add a mark command, "mark INDEX w/WEEK s/STATUS", which records
the student at INDEX as present or absent for their group's session
in that teaching week.

To support it, let's add:
* an Attendance class (session, status), held in a set by each student
* a Status enum (PRESENT, ABSENT) and the s/ prefix
* saving of attendance records to the data file

A student with no record for a session is unmarked, rather than having
a third status, so missing records are never mistaken for absences.
Loading the data file rejects records for another group's session,
more than one record for a session, or a session that is not stored.

Marking never creates a session, so a mistyped week cannot add a wrong
one; the error message tells the TA to create the session first.
Marking a student again overwrites the record, and the message names
the previous status so that an accidental overwrite is noticed. The
displayed list is left as it is, so that indexes stay the same.

Sessions themselves, the w/ prefix and looking up a group's session
for a week are left to the create session feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test mark command against a stub model
commitResults.messageBody:
MarkCommandTest only runs the command against a real ModelManager, so
it cannot show which model methods the command calls, and a broken
filter shows up only as two unequal models.

Let's add tests that run the command against a stub model, which holds
a fixed list of students and sessions and records each replaced
student. Any other model call fails the test, including resetting the
displayed list, which mark must not do. They check that the command:
* records attendance for exactly the student at the given index
* replaces an earlier record and names the previous status
* looks the week up in each student's own group
* changes nothing when the index or the session is invalid

commitResults.messageBody:
Person holds AB3's name, phone, email, address and
tags, and treats two persons with the same name as
the same person.

Roster identifies a student by their matriculation
number, and two students may share a name. A TA
cannot add two students named John Tan today,
while one student entered twice under different
names is accepted.

Let's add matric and group to Person, and identify
a student by matriculation number or email
instead of name.

Either field identifies a student on its own: both
are unique across students, so a duplicate of
either is the same student.

Callers of the constructor follow: add parses m/
and grp/, edit carries both over unchanged, and
storage reads and writes them.

This branch adds matric and group to Person and
defines its own Group and parseGroup.

F1 has since merged a Group class, a parseGroup
that normalizes before validating, and the grp/
prefix. Keeping both copies does not compile.

Drop this branch's Group and parseGroup, and use
the ones from F1.

F1 owns tutorial groups. Its Group requires an
already uppercased code, so parseGroup is the
only safe way to build one from user input.

Test sources still do not compile; that is fixed
in the next commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build test sources against the new Person
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonBuilder and JsonAdaptedPersonTest still call
the five-argument Person and JsonAdaptedPerson
constructors, so the test sources do not compile.

Nothing can be run or verified until they do, not
even the tests that have nothing to do with
matriculation numbers or tutorial groups.

Give PersonBuilder a default matric and group,
with withMatric and withGroup to override them,
and pass the matric and group of BENSON through
the JsonAdaptedPerson call sites.

PersonBuilder is where almost every test gets its
people, so defaults there keep the change to one
file rather than every caller.

The suite now runs: 253 tests, 43 failing. Most
fail because every typical person shares the
default matric and so counts as a duplicate.
Fixtures and assertions follow in later commits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Identify a student by matriculation number
commitResults.messageBody:
Person identifies a student by name, and the
matriculation number and tutorial group added
earlier cannot be edited.

Two students in a tutorial group may share a
name, so a TA cannot add both. The edit command
also skips its duplicate check when the identity
field cannot change, so it can quietly create
duplicates.

Identify a student by matriculation number, and
let edit change the matriculation number and the
tutorial group.

A matriculation number is unique and stable, and
making it editable restores the check edit
already had: it compares the edited student
against the rest only when the identity changes.
All three edit tests then pass with no change to
their assertions.

Email is no longer part of a student's identity,
so two students may share one. Test fixtures gain
distinct matriculation numbers, and add and edit
command strings gain the m/ and grp/ prefixes.

This branch identifies a student by matriculation
number and adds the m/ prefix.

F2 has since merged session creation with the w/
and d/ prefixes, and F5 a new find command whose
tests build their own students.

Keep every prefix from both sides, and give the
find tests distinct matriculation numbers.

Those six students were all built from the
default, so under matriculation-number identity
they counted as one student and the roster
refused to hold them.

One find assertion expected a renamed student to
disappear, which held when identity was the name.
It now checks that the record with the old name
is gone instead.
